articles.title: Why Pawan Sehrawat replaced Tajinderpal Singh Toor as India's Asian Games flag-bearer
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Tajinderpal Singh Toor will not be able to lead the Indian contingent at the Asian Games opening ceremony after the celebrated shot-putter arrived wit.
articles.body: Tajinderpal Singh Toor will not be able to lead the Indian contingent at the Asian Games opening ceremony after the celebrated shot-putter arrived without his ceremonial kit, forcing a late change in India's flag-bearers.Seasoned kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat has been named as Toor's replacement and will now join shooting star Manu Bhaker in carrying the Indian flag at Saturday's opening ceremony.The 30-year-old Sehrawat was part of the Indian men's kabaddi team that won gold at the previous Asian Games. India's chef-de-mission Sahdev Yadav confirmed the change to PTI.Toor's absence is the result of a logistical issue involving the ceremonial kit. The athlete said he was informed that his kit would reach Nagoya airport only at 3pm, making it difficult for him to collect it and still reach the opening ceremony venue on time."I am told that my ceremonial kit will reach at 3pm at the (Nagoya) airport. Reaching the opening ceremony venue after collecting my (ceremonial) kit from airport on time will be very difficult. So, I have told IOA (Indian Olympic Association) that I am not coming for opening ceremony," Toor told PTI.The athletics contingent has been stationed at the University of Tsukuba near Tokyo since September 13 for an acclimatisation camp. The team is scheduled to travel to Nagoya on September 21, two days before the athletics events begin.The athletes were not originally expected to participate in either the opening or closing ceremonies, which is why they did not have the ceremonial kits with them."They will be leaving Nagoya on September 30, one day after the end of athletics competition and four days before the closing ceremony (on October 4)," a team official said.Toor confirmed that the ceremonial kits were not with the athletics contingent."Nobody in athletics team has ceremonial kits with them," he revealed.The 75-member athletics contingent, however, has received its official competition kits. Multiple members of the group confirmed this to PTI.Meanwhile, Manu Bhaker's selection as the women's flag-bearer was widely expected given her achievements on the international stage.Bhaker created history at the 2024 Paris Olympics by becoming the first athlete from Independent India to win two medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games. She claimed bronze in both the individual and mixed team 10m air pistol events.At the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, athletics was India's biggest medal contributor with 29 medals, including six gold, 14 silver and nine bronze. Shooting produced 22 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and six bronze.India finished that edition with a record 106 medals overall, including 28 gold.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Maybe 32': Anju Bobby George hopeful of more athletics medals despite Neeraj Chopra miss at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: The absence of Neeraj Chopra may have taken away Indian athletics’ biggest individual name, but former long jumper Anju Bobby George believ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The absence of Neeraj Chopra may have taken away Indian athletics’ biggest individual name, but former long jumper Anju Bobby George believes it need not take away from the athletics contingent’s medal ambitions at the Asian Games. The 2003 Paris World Championships bronze medallist expects India’s track and field contingent to cross the 30-medal mark.India won 29 athletics medals — six gold, 14 silver and nine bronze — at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, its best-ever medal haul in the sport at the continental showpiece. “Neeraj is a big name in athletics, with multiple world-level medals. It is very unfortunate that he is not in our team this time because of an ankle injury. Yes, that’s a setback,” Anju told TOI in an exclusive interview. “But definitely we have many other athletes who are performing well. This time, we are expecting more than last time — more than 30, maybe 32.”For Anju, the defining feature of the current athletics squad is its breadth. Rather than relying on one or two medal contenders, there are podium possibilities across disciplines, particularly the jumps, middle and long-distance events and relays. “This is the beauty of our athletics contingent this time. If you take any event, we are aiming for medals,” she said.The women’s long jump could be one of the most intriguing contests for India in Aichi-Nagoya, with Ancy Sojan and Shaili Singh both entering as serious medal hopes. Ancy, in June this year, jumped 6.88m in Bhubaneswar to break Anju’s 22-year-old national record of 6.83m.“Records are always meant to be broken because that is the path, that’s the growth,” she said. “Otherwise, after I got the World Championships medal, nobody else would’ve done such wonderful achievements for Indian athletics. Ancy is now seasoned, she’s fixed and she’s performing. Shaili is also jumping above 6.80m, but she is yet to set her approach and rhythm and is committing fouls. Otherwise, both jumpers are equally good. We are expecting gold and silver. Either Ancy or Shaili will win gold.”In men’s long jump, Murali Sreeshankar provides another compelling comeback story. The 27-year-old, who missed the Paris Olympics after suffering a patellar tendon rupture in 2024, has returned to top level and produced an 8.38m season-best in June — the second-best jump of his career behind his 8.41m national record.“He is such a tremendous athlete. He was nowhere last year because of the injury. We wonder how he came back, how he conquered again. After injuries, especially in jumps and that too in the take-off leg, coming back is such a big, big thing. He did that with his mental strength,” Anju said.(Watch Asian Games live & exclusive on Sony Sports and Sony LIV)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Two Asian Games medals in sight as Quimcy D’Souza, one of the pioneers of teqball in India, leads  charge
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: Quimcy D’Souza, one of the pioneers of teqball in India, stormed into the semifinals of the sport that is making its Asian Games debut here.Qu.
articles.body: NAGOYA: Quimcy D’Souza, one of the pioneers of teqball in India, stormed into the semifinals of the sport that is making its Asian Games debut here.Quimcy will face Indonesia’s Sumaya in Saturday’s semifinal, and a win will ensure the first-ever medal for India in teqball, a combination of football and table-tennis played over a curved table.The world No. 24 pulled off a major upset in her Group A women’s singles opener, defeating the top-seed, world No. 7 Yuina Sakamoto of Japan 2-1. After losing the first set 10-12, Quimcy fought back to take the next two 12-11, 13-11 to win in 43 minutes. She followed that up with a 12-9, 12-7 win over Cambodia’s DY Koemyean in just 24 minutes to book her place in the last four.Quimcy had earned a bye in the quarterfinals by virtue of topping her group. If the 24-year-old loses her semifinal to the Indonesian, she will still have a shot at a bronze on Sunday.Quimcy and Mohammed Anas Beg, meanwhile, lost their mixed doubles quarterfinals but won the repechage round 2-0 against Philippines and will now fight for the bronze.The Indian duo lost 0-2 (7-12 10-12) against Vietnam’s Hoang Minh Tan Nguyen and Gia Nghi Trinh in the quarterfinals.Bengaluru-based Quimcy was first drawn to the sport after watching videos of former Brazil football star Ronaldinho playing it. She quit her Mumbai job and moved to B’luru to set up a teqball facility, where she also coaches. “All the four years I have been playing the sport, I’ve only been explaining what it is. But the Asian Games is a huge opportunity for us,” Quimcy told TOI on Thursday.Manu, Toor to be flagbearersShooter Manu Bhaker and shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor have been named flag bearers of the Indian contingent for Saturday’s opening ceremony. For Toor, it will be another moment of pride after he successfully defended his Asian Games title in Hangzhou. “I’m very proud to be named the flag bearer. It is a moment of great pride for me to be named a flag bearer along with an Olympic medallist (Bhaker),” said ToorGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dallas Trinity FC downs Fort Lauderdale United, extends winning streak to three
articles.summary: The victory moves Trinity FC into third place in the Gainbridge Super League standings.
articles.body:
Dallas Trinity FC defeated Fort Lauderdale United, 2-1, on Friday at Beyond Bancard Field, picking up its third straight win.

Trinity FC opened the scoring in the 32nd minute with a goal from midfielder Felicia Knox, who headed the ball into the back of the net off a set piece. It was Knox's first goal of the season and gave Dallas a 1-0 lead heading into halftime.

Dallas wasted little time extending its lead after the break. Jasmine Hamid scored just 40 seconds into the second half to double her team's advantage. Fort Lauderdale cut the lead in half in the 59th minute on a goal from forward Sh'nia Gordon, but Trinity FC was able to see the match out.

"This group is very talented. It's going to take that mentality and grittiness," head coach Lee Nguyen said after the match. "I'm very pleased and proud because we had a very similar game in the first game of the year, but this time we were able to close it out. So I'm very proud of them."

The win moved Trinity FC into third place in the Gainbridge Super League standings. The team plays Lexington SC at Toyota Stadium in Georgetown, Kentucky in its next match on Sept. 25.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur Starting XI vs Aston Villa: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
articles.summary: Tottenham vs Aston Villa: Pedro Porro and Sandro Tonali Return for SpursTottenham need something tangible now. Better patterns, cleaner build-up and occasion...
articles.body:
Tottenham vs Aston Villa : Pedro Porro and Sandro Tonali Return for Spurs

Tottenham need something tangible now. Better patterns, cleaner build-up and occasional spells of control mean very little when the table still says no wins, no league goals and only four games played. Add a Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool in midweek and the picture is simple, Spurs have started badly.

There is at least some decent news before Aston Villa arrive. Pedro Porro is fit again, Sandro Tonali is available and Destiny Udogie is ready to come back into the side. For Roberto De Zerbi, that matters. He has spent the opening weeks juggling fitness problems, limiting minutes and trying to avoid another injury spiral.

Tottenham were cautious with Porro and Udogie during the 0-0 draw with Everton . Both are expected to return on Saturday, which immediately gives the back line more balance and more thrust down the flanks. Udogie already showed sharpness in the 3-1 defeat at Liverpool, even in a losing cause.

Tottenham injury update boosts key areas

Tonali's return may be the most important of the lot. The £100million midfielder missed the Anfield trip with a knock, but he is back in training and should be in the squad. Spurs have lacked authority in central areas, and his availability gives De Zerbi more control and more bite.

James Maddison is another case being handled carefully. He has yet to start a match this season, but the manager has indicated he could now get the nod. That would be timely because Tottenham's biggest problem has been obvious, they do not score enough and have created too little from good positions.

There are still absentees. Dejan Kulusevski has returned to first-team training, but will not feature yet as he builds match fitness after a long lay-off. Mykhailo Mudryk remains sidelined with an ankle injury and is not expected back until after the international break. Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons are also out.

Roberto De Zerbi needs momentum before break

The manager has already pointed to an unstructured pre-season and a squad still short physically. That rings true. Spurs have looked uneven, and the reshaped medical department has clearly preferred caution over risk. Given the injury damage of the past two seasons, that is understandable.

Aston Villa arrive with their own league problems, despite a 3-1 cup win over Coventry in midweek. This is a real chance for Tottenham to change the mood before the three-week break. Another blank, another stumble, and the noise gets louder.

Kinsky ; Porro, Van Hecke , Van de Ven , Udogie; Bentancur , Gallagher; Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush ; Solanke .

Kick-off is 12:30pm BST on Saturday, September 19 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

articles.title: Arteta backs Gyokeres: Arsenal boss insists striker’s confidence is intact and goals will come despite limited minutes
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal know the value Viktor Gyokeres can bring and has insisted the forward is not struggling for confidence.Gyokeres has featured ju...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal know the value Viktor Gyokeres can bring and has insisted the forward is not struggling for confidence.

Gyokeres has featured just once in the Premier League so far this season, a 12-minute cameo as a substitute against Chelsea earlier this month.

The Swedish striker has found himself behind Kai Havertz in Arsenal 's plans, while he has failed to take starting opportunities after underwhelming performances against Napoli and Ipswich in cup competition.

Gyokeres scored 21 goals in all competitions to finish as Arsenal's leading scorer last season, but faces an uncertain future amid limited minutes.

Speaking ahead of today's clash against Gyokeres' former club, Brighton , Arteta said there was no confidence issue with the 28-year-old. He said that Arsenal know the forward 'has the capacity to score goals'.

"No [there's no confidence issue], especially in the Premier League he hasn't played that many minutes," Arteta said in his press conference on Friday.

"Last week he played in Napoli and he had a good game. It is about moments as well and we need to give him all the support and confidence that he needs because we know the player that we have and that he has the capacity to score goals.

"The team is doing certain different things this season as well. There is nothing unique for Viktor, it is for everybody. It is my job to fit players in, find connections, and find the level of confidence for the players to give their best for the team."

Gyokeres is set to join up with Sweden for the international break, where he boasts an impressive record of 21 goals in 37 caps for the national team. Arteta said the chance of scenery could help Gyokeres rediscover his form.

"He scored a few goals [last time]. That's what a striker needs, they need minutes and goals to boost their energy."

articles.title: Josue De Paula says he'll "shut a lot of people up" with his defense
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — There was no hangover at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — There was no hangover at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.

Not after clinching the National League West. Not with the champagne still fresh in the Dodgers' minds. And certainly not with Josue De Paula getting his first real taste of the big stage in Chavez Ravine.

Instead, the Dodgers looked very much like a team preparing for October. And De Paula looked like a player who wants to be part of it.

The 21-year-old came through with the go-ahead RBI double in the sixth inning Friday night, turning a tie game into a Dodgers lead and helping spark what eventually became an 8-2 victory over the Giants.

"It felt amazing," De Paula said. "To do that for the team, give us the lead. I'm just celebrating with the boys. I just want to see us win."

That last part might have been the most telling.

De Paula isn't approaching his first week in the major leagues like a player trying to prove he belongs with a franchise full of veterans and established stars. At least publicly, he's approaching it like a kid soaking in every moment.

But his performance is making it increasingly difficult for the Dodgers to ignore what he might bring when the calendar flips to October.

Dave Roberts acknowledged as much after the game.

"He's certainly doing a lot of things well," Roberts said when asked about De Paula potentially being part of the Dodgers' postseason roster mix.

For now, De Paula says he's trying not to look too far ahead.

"Yeah, it's crossed my mind," he said of making the postseason roster. "Like I said, I try to focus on the now, right here. I'm enjoying every moment with these veteran players."

The now, on Friday, was pretty impressive.

De Paula came to the plate in the fifth inning with the Dodgers trailing 2-1 and opened the frame with a single, his first hit at Dodger Stadium.

Mookie Betts followed with a single of his own, and Teoscar Hernández brought De Paula home with an RBI single to tie the game.

One inning later, De Paula was back in the middle of it.

This time, he delivered the biggest swing of the night to that point, lining an RBI double to put the Dodgers ahead.

A player who had spent years dreaming about moments like this had just created one.

"It was awesome," De Paula said of his first week in the majors. "Like I said, everybody, the manager, all the teammates have been amazing and accepting me."

There is, however, one part of his game De Paula knows still needs work.

His defense. And he's not shying away from it.

"I know that's a big area and improvement for me," De Paula said. "I know I got a lot of hate on it. So I'm that type: if I get hate on it, I'm gonna focus on it more. So I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon."

So is the willingness to accept criticism and use it as motivation.

The Dodgers don't need De Paula to become a finished product overnight. They need to determine whether his offensive impact, approach and overall upside give them enough reason to keep him around as they prepare for a postseason run.

And his teammates are already noticing what he does at the plate.

Betts, who knows something about making an impression in a Dodgers uniform, spoke highly of De Paula's at-bats.

"He's swinging at strikes, taking balls, impacting the ball," Betts said. "There's no matchup that is really a bad matchup, which is really neat to see someone so young that can handle it…. He's been awesome."

That might be the most encouraging part of De Paula's arrival.

The results are one thing. The at-bats are another.

He's not simply getting by on raw talent. He's showing an ability to recognize strikes, lay off pitches outside the zone and impact the baseball against major-league pitching.

And on a night when the Dodgers needed a spark, he provided it.

Of course, De Paula wasn't the only Dodger putting on a show.

Betts got the night started with a leadoff home run in the first inning, crushing the second pitch he saw from Giants left-hander Cesar Perdomo, a 93 mph fastball, into the left-field pavilion.

It was the 33rd leadoff home run of Betts' career.

Later, after the Giants briefly took control, Betts came back with another home run in the eighth inning, his second of the night and his 22nd of the season.

That's two more home runs than he hit last season, with eight games remaining.

Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker then went back-to-back, before Will Smith joined the party.

Four Dodgers, Muncy, Tucker, Betts and Smith, homered in the eighth inning.

What began as a competitive game suddenly became a rout. Muncy's home run gave him 29 for the season, while Tucker continued to show signs of heating up at precisely the time the Dodgers want their lineup clicking.

But none of that changes what made Friday night particularly interesting.

The Dodgers already know what Betts, Muncy, Tucker and Smith can do. They are still learning what De Paula can become.

And on his first night in the big-league spotlight at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium, he gave them another reason to keep watching.

After Betts gave the Dodgers an early 1-0 lead, Glasnow surrendered a solo home run to Jung Hoo Lee in the second inning before Jonah Cox's RBI single put San Francisco ahead in the third.

He finished with six innings, allowing three hits and two runs while walking two and striking out 10 on 98 pitches, 63 of them for strikes.

The bullpen took it from there, while the Dodgers' offense eventually turned a close game into another comfortable victory.

They are now 94-60 on the season and remain two games behind Milwaukee for the top seed in the National League, while building a four-game cushion over Atlanta for third place.

The division has already been won. The real work is beginning now.

De Paula says he's focused on the present.

The Dodgers, meanwhile, have to be thinking about the future.

Because if Friday was any indication, Josue De Paula isn't simply here to experience the major leagues.

He's here to make it increasingly difficult to send him anywhere else.

articles.title: Josue De Paula’s 3 walk-up songs and a big double mark his memorable Dodger Stadium debut
articles.summary: Josue De Paula made plenty of noise during his first week in the major leagues with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and that's not even counting his use of three wa...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Josue De Paula made plenty of noise during his first week in the major leagues with the Los Angeles Dodgers , and that's not even counting his use of three walk-up songs in the same game.

"It was awesome," he said, flashing a dazzling smile.

Batting ninth as the designated hitter, De Paula went 2 for 3 with two runs and an RBI in his Dodger Stadium debut Friday night, an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants .

"I have the utmost confidence in myself and belief," he said, "so I know when the moment is up for it, I know I'm going to come through."

De Paula debuted in the major leagues last Friday at Miami . In eight games, the 21-year-old has five hits — his first being a three-run homer off Eury Pérez of the Marlins — five RBIs and four runs. He's drawn eight walks and struck out just twice. He's hitting .238 with an OPS of .924.

"We knew that coming up to the big leagues he wasn't going to get overwhelmed," manager Dave Roberts said.

De Paula got called up after four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani went on the injured list and is playing his way into a shot at making the postseason roster.

"We need to have somebody coming off the bench. He's in the mix," Roberts said. "He's certainly doing a lot of things well."

De Paula was born and raised in Brooklyn, but relocated to his father's native Dominican Republic when the COVID-19 pandemic shut down sports in New York so he could play baseball year-round. He lived with his uncles and enrolled in a baseball academy.

He gained Dominican citizenship, which allowed him to sign with the Dodgers as an international free agent in 2022. He was quickly promoted to Class A the following year at age 18. In 2024, he was promoted to High-A.

Last year, he represented the Dodgers in the All-Star Futures Game , hitting a three-run homer and earning MVP honors.

De Paula is the first player to be called up directly from Double-A during Andrew Friedman's 12-year tenure as president of baseball operations. He's also the first player in Dodgers history to wear No. 95.

Unofficially, he may be the first player on the team to use three different walk-up songs in the same game. In a nod to his Brooklyn roots — also the New York borough where the Dodgers originated — he came to the plate in the second inning to "Notorious" by The Notorious B.I.G., another Brooklyn native.

"I didn't expect the fans to be so supportive and they were awesome," he said.

De Paula led off the fifth to "Ima a Boss" by rapper Meek Mill in a nod to his father and promptly singled for his first hit at home. He got the ball and planned to give the keepsake to his parents. His third walk-up song was for his mother.

His two-out double in the sixth snapped a 2-all tie.

"I just love his at-bats," Roberts said. "He takes his walks. When the ball's in the hitting zone, he can slug you — but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."

De Paula even won his challenge using the Automated Ball-Strike system during one at-bat.

"I feel the adrenaline, but I just feel like I know how to pinpoint it and focus it," he said. "I'm so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down."

De Paula displays a solid swing and an instinct for good pitch selection. Defensively, he knows he needs some work in the outfield.

"I'm going to shut a lot of people up on my defense very soon," he said.

De Paula has already impressed Dodgers teammate and former AL MVP Mookie Betts , who called it "really neat" to see a young player who can handle any opposing pitcher.

"He loves playing the game," Betts said. "When he gets on the field, it's like a quiet focus, but when he's off the field, he likes joking and laughing. He's a good kid."

articles.title: 🧨 Koop at risk, Cardinale lucky charm, Martinez agent 🗣️ morning news☀️
articles.summary: After the Monza vs Sassuolo clash, which lifted the curtain, the fifth round of the Serie A season continues. It’s Roma vs Inter day, the showdown between th...
articles.body:
After the Monza vs Sassuolo clash, which lifted the curtain, the fifth round of the Serie A season continues. It's Roma vs Inter day, the showdown between the two teams at the top of the table.

While waiting for the big match at the Olimpico — and the other fixtures of the fifth round — let's take a look at the most important morning news involving Serie A's biggest clubs.

Juventus , Vicario and Bremer return: Koopmeiners at risk

Juventus are preparing several changes compared to the 5-0 European win over NEC. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Vicario should reclaim his place in goal after Grabara 's positive debut, while Bremer is expected to start in central defence. There should also be room for Conceição in the attacking midfield role, without changing the 3-4-2-1 chosen by Spalletti.

The most interesting selection battle is in midfield: Sarr impressed in Europe and could be confirmed ahead of Koopmeiners, against his former club Atalanta . Up front, Kolo Muani and Woltemade are competing for a starting spot after both scoring against NEC. It is not out of the question that Spalletti could use them together during the match.

Milan , Cardinale returns to San Siro: with him there, the Rossoneri don't lose

Gerry Cardinale will be at San Siro for Milan vs Lecce. As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, the return of the Rossoneri owner had already been planned and is not linked to the Europa League defeat against Benfica.

So far, his presence has coincided with an interesting stat: in the four league matches he has attended in person this season, against Torino , Venezia, Juventus and Lazio , Milan have picked up two wins and two draws. The Rossoneri will try to extend that positive run after their first defeat of the season.

Inter, Martinez's agent: "All goalkeepers make mistakes"

Josep Martinez has received another call-up to the Spain squad. Interviewed by FcInterNews, his agent Sergio Barila underlined the significance of the achievement: «He should enjoy a well-deserved call-up, he worked very hard to earn it». The agent also reaffirmed his confidence in the goalkeeper's ability, now Inter's first choice.

Barila also responded to criticism after the mistake against Real Madrid , reminding everyone that all great goalkeepers can make errors and that the role exposes players to especially harsh judgment. There is also no concern about the competition with Provedel : according to the agent, it is a normal situation at a club of Inter's level.

Napoli , Gilmour wins over Allegri: third straight start in Florence?

Billy Gilmour is preparing for a possible third consecutive start, after Arsenal and Bologna . According to Corriere dello Sport, Massimiliano Allegri intends to keep the Scottish midfielder alongside Lobotka in the 4-2-3-1, forming a partnership capable of alternating between build-up play and forward runs.

After a season marked by injuries, Gilmour is making the most of this new opportunity to carve out a more important role. Tempo, precision and the ability to play vertically are the qualities convincing Allegri: against Fiorentina , another start could be on the way.

Roma, Friedkin at the Olimpico for Inter: ownership keeping a close eye on the big match

Ryan Friedkin is expected in the capital to watch Roma vs Inter. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the Giallorossi vice-president will head to the Olimpico for the 6 p.m. match, one of the team's first direct showdowns of the season under Gasperini.

His arrival will be preceded by that of Ed Shipley, a trusted Dan Friedkin associate, who arrived in Rome around 48 hours earlier. The ownership will therefore closely follow an important fixture to assess the Giallorossi's progress at the start of the league campaign.

Lazio, Flaminio, new meeting with city hall: the project moves forward

Lazio continue working on the project for the new Stadio Flaminio. According to Corriere dello Sport, after contacts over the past month with Rome's city hall, another operational meeting is scheduled for next week to examine changes to the project and the requirements set by the heritage authority.

Among the issues still to be resolved are preserving Nervi's canopy and the need to avoid fully covering the stadium's outer facade. The next step will be the declaration of public interest, first by the city executive and then by the Capitoline Assembly, followed by the decisive Services Conference.

Fiorentina, Vanoli gets Dragusin and Atta back: Pellegrino challenges Beto

Good news for Fiorentina ahead of the match against Napoli. According to Corriere dello Sport, Dragusin and Atta have recovered from their respective physical problems and are candidates to start. Vanoli is expected to go with a 4-2-3-1, with Dragusin alongside Ranieri in defence and the Fagioli-Ndour pairing in midfield.

In attacking midfield, there should be room for Mastantuono , Atta and Njie. The main doubt concerns the centre-forward: Pellegrino, coming off three goals in his last three matches, is slightly ahead of Beto. The decision will come after the final training session.

articles.title: Michael Carrick searches for much needed win against side who have been kind to United over the years
articles.summary: 1Manchester United travel to Craven Cottage looking for a much-needed win over Fulham.The Red Devils have faced off against Fulham 96 times, winning an impre...
articles.body:
Manchester United travel to Craven Cottage looking for a much-needed win over Fulham .

The Red Devils have faced off against Fulham 96 times , winning an impressive 59.

There have also been 21 draws and 16 wins for the Cottagers in history.

Here are three storylines to get the blood pumping.

Carrick started the season in a wonderful position, having guided the side to third place in the league as interim.

Nonetheless, since his job was made permanent, form has dipped massively, with United losing two matches on the bounce at home to Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion .

With teams set to enter the international break after this weekend's round of fixtures, Carrick and United will be desperate for a win to ease the media pressure surrounding his job.

Carrick has downplayed the recent form and concerns over his job, but a loss this weekend would certainly test his confidence.

United may not be in the best of form, but they certainly have an impressive record against the Cottagers.

They won 3-2 at Old Trafford last season and drew 1-1 last season in London.

Nonetheless, in their last 20 Premier League matches, Fulham have won just once, in February 2024.

In this time, there have been 15 wins for United and just four draws.

United's Slovenian forward Sesko has scored two goals this season, one against Everton and one against Sabah in the Champions League.

Nonetheless, he has looked short of confidence and was unconvincing once again against Brighton midweek in the EFL Cup exit.

He has struggled for a starting spot in the Premier League and has been made to be content with a spot on the bench.

Last season, he scored an epic winner versus Fulham with an incredible goal in front of the Stretford End, and he will be hoping for another big moment in this match.

articles.title: A 'perfect storm' buried Philo football in a loss at West. Here's how.
articles.summary: Philo football carried a load of momentum into its Week 5 game at West Muskingum, but it didn't last long.
articles.body:
FALLS TOWNSHIP — A storm rolled through West Muskingum Athletic Booster Stadium the evening of Sept. 18, but it didn't come from the sky.

On this occasion, it arrived in the form of quarterback Noah Morrison and a revved-up Tornado defense that didn't let visiting Philo breathe in the first half in their first meeting in three years. The latter forced three turnovers before the bands took the field.

The Electrics cut a 28-point deficit in half in the third quarter, but the previously inflicted damage was too much. West emerged with a 42-21 win, its third straight since a Week 2 loss at Fort Frye evened its record.

A game that took 3 hours, 15 minutes to complete featured eight turnovers, 17 penalties and 730 offensive yards.

Morrison's return from an elbow injury, suffered during summer basketball, kept him on the shelf for almost two months as sophomore backup Jake Welch led the team to a 2-1 record in his absence.

Morrison, the returning starter, has added a new dimension.

After passing for 231 yards in a Week 4 rout of Maysville, Morrison threw touchdown passes of 32 yards to Myles Wakefield and 25 to Carter Smith in a 21-point first quarter that was the equivalent of a horror film for the Philo faithful in attendance.

West forced two punts and two turnovers in Philo territory in that span — the first led to Wakefield's TD, the second to Smith's. West held a 154-24 edge in yards by then, which grew to 306-42 by halftime.

Morrison, who later hit a leaping Smith on an 11-yard TD for the game's final score, finished 17-of-32 passing for 218 yards, with Dollings grabbing eight of those aerials for 62 yards.

West coach Nathan Brownrigg said that his return has opened up the offense, production aided by Smith and Dollings, who he said are "playing at a really high level right now."

"Jake did a great job for us for over three weeks, but Noah's athleticism, it's a little bit more being a year older," Brownrigg said. "Just the overall maturity, he provided a little bit of a spark the last couple of weeks."

That spark came in the form of Morrison's running in the second half, particularly after the game tightened.

Three of his 10 carries were third-down scrambles that moved the chains on a 10-play scoring drive in the third quarter, after Philo got within 28-14. He also had an 18-yard scramble on that drive, which set up Dente Tyson's 4-yard touchdown that made it 35-14 in the final minute.

"He was the difference maker in this game," Philo coach Dirk Lincicome said of Morrison.

Lincicome, whose team took down Tri-Valley in an emotional comeback in Week 4, said he couldn't recall a game in his 16-year career as the school's head coach when his team had as many turnovers. He called the first quarter meltdown "a perfect storm."

Smith's 65-yard touchdown run off a reverse in the second quarter pushed the deficit to 28-0 in a fitting capper to his big first half. Lincicome praised his team for clawing back, even as the odds were all but insurmountable.

Audie Buchanan's 47-yard touchdown pass over the top to K.J. Philip got Philo on the board early in the third, and an Adam Philip interception led to Sprankle's 40-yard scoring burst two plays later. It was still 35-21 after Buchanan's scramble for a score in the fourth.

"You get down in a hole like that, and all you can ask is that your kids fight as hard as they can, and they did," Lincicome said. "We won the third quarter. … When we got within two scores, I'm thinking, 'there is a lot of ball game left.'"

Sprankle needed 115 yards to reach 1,000 for the season and got just enough — on 27 carries. Most came after halftime, as West's combination of strong containment and aggressive pursuit made for a rare night of tough sledding for the MVL's second-leading rusher. Brownrigg praised his unit's aggression.

Buchanan finished 11-of-25 passing with four interceptions — Dollings snagged two.

"The best thing about tonight is that it's over," Lincicome said. "It doesn't kill our league championship hopes. All of our goals are still in front of us. I mean, this certainly doesn't help in the playoff picture, because you've got to win games, but we'll bounce back."

articles.title: Week 5 high school football roundup, Southeast upsets Crestview
articles.summary: Our Week 5 high school football roundup includes Southeast picking up a huge win over Crestview, Aurora snapping a skid and Garfield staying perfect.
articles.body:
In addition to our coverage of Streetsboro-Roosevelt , here's a look at what happened in other Portage County high school football games in Week 5:

The Pirates picked up one of the biggest upsets of the week, avenging last year's 42-0 loss to the Rebels.

While Southeast coach Pat Youel felt confident his team could overcome the odds — Drew Pasteur's Fantastic 50 had Crestview as a 28-point favorite — his team had to overcome injuries to Liam McCann and Bruce Nelson. The Pirates overcame the week's tough injury luck with a huge start, taking a 21-0 lead.

The Rebels (1-4, 0-2 Mahoning Valley Athletic Conference Gray Tier) got back into it with a lengthy touchdown drive going into halftime, then blocked a punt en route to a third-quarter touchdown to draw within 21-14. Crestview tied the game before the third quarter was through, helped by a long punt return.

Knotted at 21 midway through the fourth quarter, the Pirates (2-3, 2-0) took over thanks to a powerful ground-and-pound drive that included plenty of strong runs by Drake Longgood and Tyler Shaw, capped by a Shaw touchdown plunge.

"We stepped up big in the fourth quarter, got a couple big stops and we got the ball back with about seven minutes to go and we just went on a drive for the ages," Youel said. "[It was] Drake Longgood, Tyler Shaw and our offensive line, nothing fancy, nothing pretty. We ran iso and I probably called iso six to eight times in a row and we went down the field, chipped away and punched it in with two minutes to go in the game."

Longgood and Shaw ran behind a powerful offensive line consisting of Seth Besaw, Connor Buchkoski, Daniel Clint, Ethan Fox, Aidan McCann and Matt Neer.

"Our offensive line was just amazing on that drive," Youel said. "They just really were."

Alaunte Massrock had the other three touchdowns, all on the ground, for the Pirates.

Kicker Hannah Timmons scored her 100th career point as part of a dominant effort for the G-Men (5-0, 2-0 MVAC Gray). Max Bultrowicz got Garfield going with a 29-yard pick-six with Ryder Cain adding a three-yard touchdown run before the opening quarter was through. The G-Men left no doubt with a 33-point second quarter that included Collin McGranahan recording his own pick-six along with a 60-yard touchdown run. Garfield ran for over a first down per carry with 32 rushes for 375 yards, led by Cain's seven carries for 125 yards and two touchdowns. The G-Men also held the Golden Flashes to negative-eight yards.

The Greenmen snapped a three-game skid with a commanding performance. Mathew Huth set the tone with a 60-yard touchdown run midway through the opening quarter. Carter Fitzgerald added a touchdown run minutes into the second quarter for Aurora (2-3, 1-1 Suburban American). Tommy Stenger ran in the last two touchdowns, one apiece in the second and third quarters, for the Greenmen. Huth had a team-high 94 rushing yards on nine carries while Stenger had 10 carries for 65 yards. Fitzgerald had a monstrous game on both ends of the field, tallying nine tackles, four tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries on defense. Aurora shut Twinsburg out over the first three quarters, with the Greenmen's defensive heroics also including a Luke Hilditch interception.

Quarviyon Siggers-Greco found the end zone four times in the first quarter — first for a touchdown to give the Wildcats a 6-0 lead, then on three two-point conversions (two rushing and one passing). Siggers-Greco had seven carries for 104 yards and the touchdown while Caileb Tompkins had 15 carries for 61 yards and a touchdown. Landen Williams took a fumble to the house as part of Mogadore's 30 first-quarter points while Maddox Smith found Collin Hendrickson for a 24-yard touchdown pass as part of the Wildcats' early rush. Jackson Wallace added a 62-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter for Mogadore (4-1).

The Rovers (2-3, 0-2 Chagrin Valley Conference Valley Division) fell despite four touchdowns (two rushing, two passing) from Blake Mullaly. The Rootstown senior quarterback completed 13 of 20 passes for 266 yards and added 19 carries for 113 yards on the ground. Max McEwuen (five catches, 70 yards) and Grayson Rantilla (five catches, 84 yards, one touchdown) were primary targets for Mullaly. With Chagrin Falls leading 28-13, Mullaly knotted the score with a one-yard touchdown run, a point-after attempt, a 78-yard touchdown pass to Kiel Reuting and a two-point conversion toss to Rantilla. But the Tigers (4-1, 2-0) surged ahead on Max Frankel's one-yard touchdown run with 2:23 remaining. Will Flannery (21 carries, 114 yards) and Brady Kaas added two touchdowns apiece for Chagrin Falls.

No further details were reported on the following games:

St. Mary Central Catholic 49, Windham 12

articles.title: Incredible genius will become Liverpool's next sporting director
articles.summary: Liverpool's next sporting director could be an absolute genius. The Richard Hughes era is over at Anfield. He has left the club after a whirlwind two years....
articles.body:
Liverpool 's next sporting director could be an absolute genius.

The Richard Hughes era is over at Anfield. He has left the club after a whirlwind two years. During his time at Liverpool, Hughes attracted some of the biggest names in world football to the club.

He broke Liverpool's transfer record multiple times.

Ultimately, he signed exciting players. However, he also left the current squad quite imbalanced. When you look at Andoni Iraola 's options at right-back, it's scarce.

On the right-wing, he has to play players who prefer to play on the left because right now the Reds do not have a recognised right-winger.

All of these details and the results on the pitch juxtaposed by the mass spending have tarnished Hughes' reputation.

The success of his time will not be judged now but many years into the future. Hughes' signings could still become incredible players at the club.

But Liverpool are now planning for a future without Hughes.

This, combined with the fact that there are new minority stakeholders at the club in 1892 Holdings led by Amit Bhatia, means Liverpool's search is going to look a little different this time around.

A lot of the conversations has been around potential internal hires. Julian Ward, who has been sporting director in the past has been identified as a potential candidate. David Woodfine and Pedro Marques are another.

But the obvious choice is an external candidate.

Why Lee Dykes is destined to be Liverpool's next sporting director

The BBC has already reported that Liverpool have held talks with Brentford 's Head of Recruitment Lee Dykes.

He is someone who has been on Liverpool's radar for a while, even when the Reds were looking for a new sporting director back in 2024, Dykes was already being looked at.

At the time Michael Edwards opted with Richard Hughes. But this time around, Dykes feels like the perfect candidate and the natural solution to Liverpool's problems.

Dykes has done brilliant work at Brentford. He is recognised as a genius within the game and he's built a team consistently year after year that has been able to challenge at the upper end of the table - all while losing some of the club's best players every summer.

The Brentford man just feels like someone who is ready to make the step-up to a higher level and Liverpool is a very obvious next destination in his career as well.

articles.title: Where to watch Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo: Live stream, TV channel & start time for 2026 boxing fight
articles.summary: Here’s how to watch Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo, including streaming options and channel to catch the main card.
articles.body:
Isaac Cruz is in line for big fights next year. First, the interim WBC super lightweight champion must defend his title against Nestor Bravo.

Here's how to watch Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo, including streaming options and channel to catch the main card.

Where to watch Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo

Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo will be available on DAZN worldwide.

A DAZN monthly subscription is $24.99 on a 12-month contract or $34.99 month-to-month. The annual subscription is $249.99.

You can also sign up for the DAZN Ultimate package, which can be purchased for $49.99 per month on a 12-month contract or $449.99 per year.

DAZN Ultimate is DAZN's premium subscription tier, which includes a minimum of 12 PPV boxing events and more than 185 fights per year.

Main event start time (approx.): 11 p.m. ET | 8 p.m. PT

Location: Pechanga Arena - San Diego, California

Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo is on Saturday, September 19 in San Diego. The main card starts at 8 p.m. ET and the main event should begin around 11 p.m. ET, depending on how long the undercard fights last.

Cruz (28-3-2) beat Rolando Romero in March 2024 to become the WBA super lightweight champion, but he lost it a few months later against Jose Valenzuela. "Pitbull" bounced back and won the interim WBC title. He recently faced Lamont Roach, with the fight ending in a draw.

Back in action, the Mexican with 18 wins via knockout aims to fight the likes of Dalton Smith (or Alberto Puello if he wins when they face off), Ryan Garcia, Gary Antuanne Russell, and more. However, he's not looking past his opponent.

"Bravo is a very tough fighter who always comes forward and likes to put on a show," said Cruz. "We're going to be the next chapter of a great boxing rivalry, and I know that this fight has everything it takes to go down in history as one of the great fights in the Mexico vs. Puerto Rico rivalry.

"I expect Bravo to come out with an aggressive mindset, but we have our own strategy to counter his style."

Bravo (24-1) is 3-1 in his last four fights. He took out Pedro Campa in January to earn a shot at gold. The Puerto Rican has 17 wins via the power punch.

articles.title: Miami football news: Why Mario Cristobal isn't too worried about 'sloppy' end vs. Wake Forest
articles.summary: Mario Cristobal watched his offense score on nearly every possession for a half, then watched it disappear entirely. Speaking with Scott Van Pelt on SportsC...
articles.body:
Mario Cristobal watched his offense score on nearly every possession for a half , then watched it disappear entirely. Speaking with Scott Van Pelt on SportsCenter after No. 5 Miami's 33-20 win at Wake Forest on Friday night , the Hurricanes coach was not interested in treating the ending as a crisis.

"I like the fact that even though it got sloppy at the end, we did play complementary football," Cristobal said after the game . "In the first half, the offense was on fire. After the first drive, the defense really turned it on. And then we found ourselves a little bit banged up, but we've got to be able to overcome that."

His point was that the two units traded responsibility. When Miami's offense went cold with a string of three-and-outs, the defense produced a safety and Ethan O'Connor's late interception to close the game out. "When you go on the road and you're playing in the conference, you've got to find a way to win," Cristobal said. "We have some things to clean up, so we're looking forward to doing that."

The injuries are the real concern. Cristobal acknowledged Miami got banged up at running back and tackle, and that reserves suddenly faced a workload they had not seen through two blowouts. "We hadn't played more than 35, 38 plays in our first couple of games because of the margin in the first half," he said. "So tonight, we were tested a little bit there."

He confirmed Malachi Toney's reps were managed after halftime . "He got a little bit banged up. We don't think it's too serious," Cristobal said of the receiver, who finished with 11 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. He also credited Wake Forest for adjusting well in the second half.

On Darian Mensah , who opened 24-for-24 and finished 30-of-34 with three scores , Cristobal pointed to command rather than arm talent. "His consistency, the way he can master the offense, the way he could put us in good plays," he said, praising Mensah's pocket awareness and ability to fit throws into tight windows.

Miami is 3-0 and hosts Central Michigan next Saturday.
